name: expanding-cards
title: Expanding cards
description: Cards that open into an immersive detail view, with shared geometry and a drag-to-dismiss gesture.

preview.headline:
Stay curious.
Go a little deeper.

interaction: Tap a card to open its details. Drag downward to dismiss, or use the close button.
accessibility: Native buttons expose card actions. Expanded content hides the underlying cards from VoiceOver. A labeled close button and Escape accessibility action provide alternatives to dragging. Reduce Motion removes spring interpolation.
integration: Supply Identifiable items and one content builder. The builder receives the item and its expanded state. Keep card IDs stable and unique. Place the component in a container with enough vertical room for the expanded content. It is an inline expanding surface, not a system modal sheet.

name: morphing-sheet
title: Morphing sheet
description: A draggable surface that interpolates its height and corner radius, then settles into a compact or expanded state.
interaction: Drag the handle upward to expand the surface. Tap the handle to toggle without dragging.
accessibility: The handle is a labeled native button. VoiceOver users can also adjust the surface with increment and decrement actions. Reduce Motion disables spring interpolation. This is an inline surface, not a replacement for the focus containment of a system sheet.
integration: Bind HugsySheetPosition to your screen state. Supply compact and expanded heights and content that adapts to the current position. Dragging is limited to the handle so content can keep its own gestures. Use native .sheet presentation if your app requires a modal barrier.

name: radial-menu
title: Radial menu
description: A floating action menu with a rotating trigger, staggered spring entrances, and an arc of reachable actions.
interaction: Open the action menu, then choose an action. The actions spring outward in sequence and collapse after selection.
accessibility: Every action is a labeled native button. Collapsed actions are removed from hit testing and accessibility. The trigger announces expanded or collapsed state. Reduce Motion removes travel interpolation and trigger rotation.
integration: Supply stable, unique action IDs and main-actor closures. Use three or four actions to keep targets separated. Reserve the component's full width and height in the layout. Actions close the menu before running their closures.

name: toast-stack
title: Toast stack
description: Notifications that enter with a spring, reflow around a dismissal, and cancel their lifetime tasks when removed.
interaction: Add a notification, then dismiss one from the stack. New notifications expire independently.
accessibility: Each notification has a labeled dismiss button. Reduce Motion uses opacity rather than sliding transitions. Keep important errors in persistent screen content instead of relying on a timed toast.
integration: Keep a HugsyToasts instance in @State and overlay HugsyToastStack inside your safe area. At most four notifications remain visible. Each mounted row owns its timeout task, which is cancelled when that row disappears.

name: fluid-tabs
title: Fluid tabs
description: A shared selection pill that travels between variable-width labels with an interruptible spring.
interaction: Switch between labels. The selection pill follows your finger and settles into the next tab.
accessibility: Native buttons announce their selected state and maintain a minimum height of 44 points. Labels can scroll horizontally. Reduce Motion disables selection interpolation.
integration: Bind the selected label to your own content state. Duplicate labels are removed while preserving order. If the current selection no longer exists, the component selects the first available label. Keep labels concise and localize them in your app.

name: stretchy-header
title: Stretchy header
description: An overscroll-aware header that expands with a pull, stays edge-to-edge, and returns with native scroll physics.
interaction: Pull downward at the top of the scroll view. The header stretches with the gesture and returns with the scroll view.
accessibility: Uses a native ScrollView with normal content order. Reduce Motion disables the extra stretching effect without disabling scrolling. Keep important header text readable rather than scaling it into an image.
integration: Provide a header and content builder. The component owns its ScrollView and named coordinate space, so do not wrap it in another vertical ScrollView. The header is clipped to its expanding bounds. Apply your own safe-area policy at the screen level.
